current_route.title: Strictly Bounded Two-Layer AR Optimization with Corrected Budget
current_route.scientific_hypothesis: A two-layer stack comprising one SiO2 and one TiO2 layer, with thicknesses bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm, can achieve an arithmetic mean reflectance below 0.03 across the 450-700 nm band at normal incidence if the optimizer finds a non-quarter-wave thickness combination that balances the spectral ripple, or if the optimal solution lies near the quarter-wave points (~98 nm for SiO2, ~60 nm for TiO2) adjusted for broadband performance.
current_route.design_principle: Minimize Fresnel reflections through destructive interference using a low-index (SiO2) and high-index (TiO2) pair. The optimization will search the continuous thickness space within hard bounds to find the global minimum for the specified objective function.
current_route.proposed_topology: Air | Layer_1 | Layer_2 | Glass (where Layer_1 and Layer_2 are assigned SiO2 and TiO2 in the optimal permutation found by the optimizer, or explicitly tested as two separate candidates if the solver requires fixed ordering. Here we request the solver to optimize the assignment and thicknesses).
design_variables: material assignment of Layer_1 and Layer_2 (permutation of SiO2/TiO2)
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (450-700 nm)
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness must remain within 40-160 nm range
theory_basis: Quarter-wave approximation as initial guess heuristic
expected_advantages: Simple two-layer structure is easy to fabricate
SiO2/TiO2 provides a large index contrast suitable for broadband AR
known_risks: Two layers may be insufficient to reach < 0.03 mean reflectance over such a wide band (450-700 nm) given the specific index values
Optimizer may get stuck in local minima if initialization is poor
current_route.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar two-layer antireflection coating. Stack definition: Incident medium Air (n=1.0), Substrate Glass (n=1.52). Exactly two finite layers: one must be SiO2 (n=1.46) and one must be TiO2 (n=2.40). The optimizer must determine the optimal stacking order (SiO2 then TiO2, OR TiO2 then SiO2) and the optimal thickness for each layer. Constraints: Each layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm inclusive. Objective: Minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at 0 degrees incidence, sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm in 5 nm steps. Solver settings: Maximum forward evaluations = 64. Random seed = 17. Method: Deterministic TMM only. Output the best candidate's stack order, thicknesses, and the full reflectance spectrum. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimized arithmetic mean power reflectance in the 450-700 nm band; mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
current_route.revision_reason: Correcting the 'CHARTER_DRIFT_ERROR' from the previous iteration where the solver evaluation budget exceeded the immutable limit of 64. The new request explicitly enforces the 64-evaluation cap and seed 17. Additionally, the request clarifies the need to explore both stacking permutations to ensure the global optimum is not missed due to a fixed-order assumption.
